scope: NICE CG84 assessment of dehydration and shock, and oral rehydration, in children under 5 with gastroenteritis.

keyRecommendations.text: Ask whether the child appears unwell, has altered responsiveness, decreased urine output, pale or mottled skin, or cold extremities.
For oral rehydration, use a low-osmolarity solution (240–250 mOsm/L) and give 50 ml/kg for deficit replacement over 4 hours plus maintenance fluid.
Measure venous acid–base status and chloride if shock is suspected or confirmed.

clinicalBottomLine: Recognise dehydration and shock from the clinical features in CG84, replace deficit with low-osmolarity ORS at 50 ml/kg over 4 hours plus maintenance when oral rehydration is used, and check acid–base and chloride if shock is suspected.
notableCaveats: The ESPGHAN/ESPID guideline suggested in the spreadsheet is not in PMC. CG84 is the open recommendation text.

source.title: Diarrhoea and vomiting caused by gastroenteritis in under 5s: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline CG84.
